label: PF Backlog 592
title: EDP-11: ResidencyPolicy/RegionResolver + RegionCell capability attestation + fail-closed tenant provisioning
body: Part of EPIC BI-PF-1292. Source: docs/Product_Forge_Enterprise_Performance_Security_DB_Storage_Roadmap.md. Phase item (see epic). Language rule L1 = Go; must pass scripts/dev/language_rule_review.py.

delivery.note: EDP-11 residency evaluator + resolver + attestation + fail-closed provisioning

brief.problem: Tenants can be provisioned without enforcing data-residency policy or verified region capability.
brief.what_adds: ResidencyPolicy evaluator, RegionResolver, RegionCell attestation checks, fail-closed provisioning.
brief.why: Enterprise and regulatory contracts require provable residency enforcement.

objective: Deliver ResidencyPolicy evaluation, RegionResolver, RegionCell capability attestation verification, and fail-closed tenant provisioning wired into enterprise tenant lifecycle.
acceptance_criteria: Tenant provisioning fails closed when residency policy or RegionCell attestation cannot be satisfied
Residency evaluation consumes versioned policy registry (BI-PF-1297) with IN-v1/US-v1 profiles
RegionResolver maps tenant to compliant RegionCell deterministically
Passes scripts/dev/language_rule_review.py
approach: Concrete residency Evaluator + RegionResolver (deterministic, capability-matched, attestation-verified) reusing the 1297 registry; Ed25519 region-cell attestation (key_id + digest + not_after) via stdlib, mirroring pfcore/license; fail-closed provisioning (internal/tenants) + a mountable http.Handler. Cells/keyring in config/residency-cells; policies in config/residency-profiles. Config.capability-packs.json NOT touched (it is the media-pack catalog).
verification: go_modules_check OK (12 modules); precheck PASS (45 gates)
tests: attestation verify (tamper/expired/unknown-key fail-closed), resolver determinism, evaluator modes, provisioning + handler fail-closed
risks: Fail-closed default could block all provisioning if attestation service is down
Counsel-owned policy content may change shape
RegionCell attestation trust model (signed claims?) undefined
rollback: Config flag to bypass attestation (audit-logged) for break-glass; policy registry rollback via version pin.

analysis.implementation_strategy: Extend the enterprise tenant provisioning path (capability_bridge/capability_packs patterns, /api/v1/enterprise/tenants) with a Go ResidencyPolicy evaluator + RegionResolver that consumes the versioned policy registry (BI-PF-1297), validates RegionCell capability attestation, and provisions fail-closed when attestation or residency match fails.
dependency_findings: REQUIRES BI-PF-1297 (state: policy registry merged, IN-v1/US-v1 profiles exist)
REQUIRES BI-PF-1302 (state: merged, structured errors + quotas available)
REQUIRES BI-PF-1301 (state: merged, tenant context/RLS for provisioning)
conflict_findings: Touches tenant provisioning endpoints also extended by BI-PF-1302 quotas - sequence after 1302
Shares capability-packs.json config with capability_bridge owners
duplication_findings: No existing residency/region resolver code found
capability_bridge.py is Python pattern reference only (L1=Go)
Policy content owned by BI-PF-1297 - do not duplicate here
analysis.rationale: Existing capability bridge and tenant provisioning provide natural extension points; residency resolution is new logic but not a new component.
assumptions: BI-PF-1297 registry exposes a machine-readable versioned API
RegionCell attestation can be verified locally or via signed endpoint
risks: Fail-closed default could block all provisioning if attestation service is down
Counsel-owned policy content may change shape
RegionCell attestation trust model (signed claims?) undefined
missing_info: Which residency decisions are hard-block vs warn

context_review.reason: Deps provide registry, errors, and tenant context; attestation verification model must be decided by the human.
